# OA.4 The endogenous pension design {#esc}

Section 7 of the paper lets the electorate choose the design $\theta$ as well as the tax rate, under a deadweight
cost of redistribution whose parameter $\lambda$ is calibrated so that the U.S. electorate re-elects its observed
design. This chapter holds the tables of that section and of its appendices, the same counterfactuals with the UK
as host, the design along the baseline path, the timing of the choice and an alternative cost specification.

## OA.4.1 The cost and the cross-country test {#esc-calibration}

The paper's two tables of section 7.3: the calibrated cost at each IES, and the designs the UK and France choose
under the U.S. parameter and under their own.

{{< include _generated/groups/esc-calibration.qmd >}}

## OA.4.2 Counterfactuals on the U.S. {#esc-us}

Each counterfactual is read twice, with the design pinned at the U.S. value and with the design chosen, and both
readings carry the cost, so the distance between them is the political response. In the paper's figure an open
marker is the pinned reading and a filled one the chosen; click either for its row.

{{< include _generated/groups/esc-us.qmd >}}

## OA.4.3 The UK as host {#esc-uk}

The same counterfactuals with the UK as host, at the UK's own cost parameter, the one at which its electorate
re-elects the UK's observed design; it lies below the U.S. parameter at an IES of one or below and above it at two.
The figure sets the two hosts side by side; the tables print the UK's numbers. On both hosts France's voting
profile moves the design most, toward flat benefits, and by less on the UK, whose own voting profile is already
flatter than the U.S. one. France's income distribution moves the two hosts' designs in opposite directions, since
on the U.S. it compresses relative incomes and on the UK it spreads them. The design response leaves the UK's tax
rate, savings rate and workweek essentially at the reading with the design pinned, so on the UK the response is
confined to the design itself.

{{< include _generated/groups/esc-uk.qmd >}}

## OA.4.4 The design along the baseline path {#esc-path}

The calibration pins the design in 2020 only; every later design is a prediction of the model. Section 7 describes
the drift of the design along the baseline path in words; here are the paths of the design and of the tax rate,
chosen and pinned, at each IES and at two other values of the Frisch elasticity $\xi$, which the paper reports in
a footnote.

## OA.4.5 The timing of the design choice {#esc-timing}

Section 7.1 shows that each timing of the choice puts the design at a corner when redistribution is costless: a
design chosen together with the tax rate re-splits benefits current retirees have already earned, a design chosen
one period ahead trades the young's redistributive stake against the forward-looking one, and a design chosen once
and for all enters every channel at once. The table reports the numerical checks of these timings.

{{< include _generated/groups/esc-timing.qmd >}}

## OA.4.6 An alternative cost specification {#esc-scale}

A cost attached to the design rather than to the transfer it performs: a flat benefit forfeits a fixed share of
revenue whatever it redistributes. The table sets it beside the paper's cost, which scales with the dispersion of
relative incomes: the calibration of each, and the design each lets the electorate choose under acute ageing and
under France's income distribution and voting patterns.
